title: nanomem v3 -- ingest-path peak RSS before and after the reserved arena

protocol.cache_provenance: built by scratch/refound/bench_competitors.py --prep; the SAME docs.npy / queries.npy / gold.json / rng(0) insertion order used by competitors_standard_results.json
protocol.phases: build = ingest, flush, close, reopen, query (the shape bench_competitors.py charges as peak_rss_delta_mb). serve = a fresh process opening the file the build left behind.
protocol.isolation: one subprocess per (arm, corpus, phase) so ru_maxrss is clean
protocol.recall: computed in the driver from each arm's returned id matrix; an arm cannot score itself
protocol.exactness: top-10 compared row by row against committed_baseline_loop, the engine exactly as committed at git 6aa6923
protocol.contention: the machine was NOT quiesced; each arm records the load average at its start and end

committed_baseline_loop.what: The committed engine, unchanged: add_fact() in a loop, nothing told to it. This is the arm competitors_standard_results.json calls nanomem_v3_exact, re-measured here on today's machine.

committed_baseline_hint.what: The committed engine plus the escape hatch that already existed and that nothing in the library called: VaultEngine.reserve_rows(n) before the loop.

reserved_view_loop.what: The reserved-view arena: add_fact() in a loop, still nothing told to the engine. This is the fix that needs no caller cooperation.

reserved_view_hint.what: The reserved-view arena plus the exact row count.

vault_add_batch.what: Through the public Vault.add_batch, which now hints the batch length for itself -- the wiring, end to end, with no benchmark-only call.

n10000.gold_rule: G[:, :2] gold paragraph indices shipped in hotpot_train_8k_embeds.npz; questions kept in file order, restricted to those whose gold indices are < n_docs, first 500

n71433.gold_rule: G[:, :2] gold paragraph indices shipped in hotpot_train_8k_embeds.npz; questions kept in file order, restricted to those whose gold indices are < n_docs, first 500

engine_stats_reopened.active_heap_ram_method: sum of the numpy buffers this vault has ALLOCATED (capacity, not just the used slice) + record bytes + a 64 B/row index estimate; never a constant. It is what the VAULT holds, not what the PROCESS costs: the interpreter, numpy itself and transient copies are not in it. MEASURED GAP, in a process that does nothing but open a vault it did not write and read stats once: 1.10x at 71,433 docs (288.9 MB of RSS growth against 262.0 MB reported) and 1.38x at 10,000 (50.7 MB against 36.8 MB) -- scratch/refound/stats_rss_gap_v3r5.json. Both sides of that gap moved when Arena.reserve became the default: the older figure (1.52x, 612.3 MB against 401.6 MB, scratch/refound/rss_v3r4.json) was measured on an arena that grew by doubling. Use 'process_rss_kb' for the process figure.

memory.method: resource.getrusage(RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss (bytes on darwin) for the peak, `ps -o rss=` for the resident value; baseline taken after the shared vectors/texts are loaded, so the delta is the engine's own footprint. Identical to the accounting in bench_competitors.py.

growth_policy.what: the allocator question with the engine taken out: a 768-d fp32 arena is grown to 71,433 rows in 50-row steps under each policy, one subprocess per policy so ru_maxrss is clean. Directly comparable to memory_results.json -> growth_policy.

directory_estimate.split: the shipped ingest_file default: 50-line chunks, 10-line overlap
directory_estimate.what: the hint ingest_directory uses before it has read anything: total bytes / BYTES_PER_CHUNK_ESTIMATE. Rows are measured by running the real split over real trees.

reference_points.read_from: winners.<corpus>.<metric>.all -- every arm that file reports, not a selection

package_fingerprint.what: sha256[:16] of each module's executable code with docstrings stripped -- see _code_sha. Writing a measured number into a docstring does not move these; changing a line of code does.

replicate.what: `runs_mb` is the loader peak of run 1 (the `summary` above) followed by 3 independent re-runs of the same build. Quote `median_mb` and `range_mb`, not a single reading.

exactness.what: SHA-256 over the concatenated fp32 score vectors of every query against every row -- the whole scan, not the top-10. Equal digests mean the reserved arena changed no number anywhere, which a latency measurement on a loaded machine cannot show.

latency_duel.what: the same vaults the build phase left on disk, re-opened and re-timed CYCLE BY CYCLE, arms always in the same order, with a bare numpy matvec measured in every cycle. The machine was NOT quiet (see load_avg): read the ratio column, not the milliseconds.

headline.what: derived from `summary` and `replicate` in this same file and from the peak_rss_delta_mb of competitors_standard_results.json. Every nanomem figure is the pair of runs, not a single reading.
headline.metric: peak ru_maxrss delta over build + reopen + 500 queries, MB

post_report_verification.what: one more build of each end of the comparison, run AFTER the report and the docstrings were written, against the ranges recorded in `replicate`.

chunked_alternative.what: the design alternative the reserved view was chosen over: holding the arena as fixed-size chunks. Same RAM story (growth never copies), no reservation needed, and the scan pays for it. Measured on the same corpora, paired in cycles.

competitors_same_harness.why: A verifier found the 10,000-document claim 'nanomem is now the LOWEST of every arm measured' to be a cross-harness comparison: nanomem's figure came from this file, the competitors' from competitors_standard_results.json, and this harness reads about 4.3% lower on the identical configuration. These arms remove the comparison from the argument by re-running the competitors HERE.
competitors_same_harness.metric: ru_maxrss delta over build + reopen + 500 queries, baseline after the shared vectors are resident -- the same metric, the same Ctx and the same insertion order as every nanomem arm in this file

verdict.finding: The cross-harness worry does not materialise. Re-run under THIS harness, the competitor arms land within 0.5 MB of their published figures at both sizes, so the ~4.3% offset seen on nanomem's own baseline arm is specific to that arm and does not contaminate the comparison.
verdict.claim_at_10000: STANDS, and is no longer cross-harness: nanomem 42.7 MB against FAISS 50.3 and sqlite-vec 53.0 measured in the same harness, same Ctx, same metric, 3 runs each with a spread of 0.1-0.2 MB.
verdict.claim_at_71433: UNCHANGED: nanomem 298.4 MB against FAISS 230.2 in-harness (1.296x) and sqlite-vec 335.8 (0.889x). FAISS still wins this axis at scale.
verdict.what_was_NOT_re_run: The four Chroma arms. nanomem is 0.21x-0.34x of them at 10,000 and 0.34x-0.45x at 71,433, margins far larger than any plausible harness offset, so those comparisons remain cross-harness by choice and are reported as such.
